html:
The longest river in North America, about 3,700 kilometres long. It rises in the Rocky Mountains of Montana, crosses the Great Plains and joins the Mississippi just above St. Louis. Its silt earned it the name "Big Muddy".

On its upper bluffs farming peoples lived in villages of earth lodges: the Mandan, the Hidatsa and the Arikara, now the Three Affiliated Tribes. Their villages were great trading centres where plains nomads swapped horses and hides for maize. Lower down lived the Missouria, who gave the river its name.

After the Louisiana Purchase, Lewis and Clark went up the river in 1804 and wintered with the Mandan. Fur traders and steamboats followed, and smallpox from a steamboat nearly wiped out the Mandan in 1837. Lower river towns became starting points of the Oregon Trail. In the 1950s the Garrison Dam flooded the best land of the Three Affiliated Tribes.
